craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as nondifference arising (abheda WITH affliction, not after). Sanskrit-first: yadā…tadā (WHEN…THEN — hinge kept; with-it, not after-it per C1); kevalam (ALONE — then-ALONE: nondifference exclusive); varṣati (RAINS — the hymn rains, kept raining). Rows: 1 (‘rains supreme nectar’ closes — verb last, nectar the landing), 9 (when/then hinge — occasion, not obstacle), 10 (nectar left standing, no gloss). Close: ‘the hymn rains supreme nectar’. Rupture: ‘then alone’ (affliction turns to nondifference — suffering is the trigger per C1, inverted expectation kept). Rejected: ‘whenever troubles come’ — killed: ārti (affliction) + mind's-reach both precise; ‘showers’ — killed: colloquial, varṣa rains; ‘my oneness with You’ — killed: abheda is nondifference (kept technical). Read aloud: when-EV-er af-FLIC-tion … COMES with-IN the MIND's-reach — THEN a-LONE, lord, MY-non-DIFF-er-ence FROM-you: the HYMN-rains su-PREME-nec-TAR.

lines: Whenever affliction, dealing slight anguish, comes within the mind’s reach —
then alone, Lord, my nondifference from You: the hymn rains supreme nectar.
l4.sanskrit_cite: mānasagocaram eti yadaiva kleśadaśā tanutāpavidhātrī nātha ! tadaiva mama tvadabhedas stotraparāmṛtavṛṣṭiḥ udeti

reads_against.argmap: What is the relation between affliction and nondifference? → Affliction is the occasion, not the obstacle: nondifference + nectar arise with it, not after it.
c1_essence: Affliction's arrival is the occasion, not the obstacle: with it comes nondifference, and nectar arises.
Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains.
It inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.
